deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page continues the previous one. Gauss is reducing observations of Juno made in spring 1815 against comparison stars, using the 1796 zone observations in Lalande's Histoire Céleste. Every star place is treated in the same way: (i) remove the 1796 aberration and nutation from Lalande's apparent place; (ii) precess the mean place to 1815; (iii) add the 1815 aberration and nutation. All products are done in 7-place logarithms; 'n' marks a negative number.

Aberration/nutation scheme (as I reconstruct it, with α = right ascension, δ = declination, ε = obliquity, ☉ = solar longitude, ☊ = longitude of the lunar node):
- Auxiliary sun angle: tan ☉' = tan ☉ / cos ε. For ☉ = 32°28' this gives ☉' = 34°45'; for ☉ = 8°19' it gives 9°4'.
- Amplitude: A = 20.25'' · sqrt(cos²☉ cos²ε + sin²☉), so log A = 1.2805 (1796) and 1.2699 (1815).
- Aberration in α: Δα = −A cos(α−☉') sec δ.
- Aberration in δ: Δδ = A sin(☉'−α) sin δ − 20.25'' cos☉ sin ε cos δ. The constant part is −6.79'' (1796) and −7.97'' (1815).
- Nutation in α: a constant term (−16.00'' in 1796, −16.36'' in 1815) plus −C cos(α−☊') tan δ, with log C = 0.8673 (1796) or 0.8601 (1815).
- Nutation in δ: −C sin(α−☊') (sign as in the log columns).
- The four log columns on the right are exactly these products. Row 3 holds log sec δ, log sin δ and log tan δ respectively.

(1) TOP: star c, observed 21 Apr 1796, reduced to 29 Mar 1815.
- Lalande apparent place: α = 192°54'31.95'' (= 12h51m38.13s), δ = +1°30'20.03''.
- 1796 corrections removed:
  - α: −17.71 (aberration), +16.00 (nutation constant), +0.02 (nutation tan δ term).
  - δ: −0.19, +6.79, −7.32.
  - Result: mean 1796 place 192°54'30.22'', +1°30'19.31''.
- Precession over t = 18.94 yr, evaluated at the mean of the two epochs (α_m ≈ 193°1.8', δ_m ≈ 1°27'):
  - log(n t) = log 18.94 + log 20.06 = 2.57980.
  - Δδ = n t cos α_m: 2.57980 + 9.98868n → −6'10.24''.
  - Δα = m t + n t sin α_m tan δ_m. Here m t = 14'31.98''; log(n t sin α_m) = 1.93284n; adding log tan δ_m = 8.40436 gives −2.17''.
- Mean 1815 place: 193°9'0.03'', +1°24'9.07''.
- 1815 corrections added:
  - α: +18.75, −16.36, +0.02.
  - δ: −0.03, −7.97, +7.18.
  - Result: c apparent = 193°9'2.44'', +1°24'8.25''.
- Right-hand log blocks give each term:
  - 1796 (☉' 34°45', ☊' 109°25', α 192°55'): sums 1.2483 → 17.71; 9.2704 → 0.19; 8.3409n → 0.02; 0.8645 → 7.32.
  - 1815 (☉' 9°4', ☊' 95°40', α 193°9'): sums 1.2689 → 18.57; 8.5111n → 0.03; 8.3636 → 0.02; 0.8564 → 7.18.

(2) Approximate apparent places of comparison stars a and b for 1815. These are carried in from elsewhere.

(3) 'Reduction der Junobeobachtungen'.
- Four determinations of Juno's α at clock times 10h51'22.4'', 48'19.0'', 35'52.6'', 38'9.2''.
- They come from stars d, c, a, b, giving 192°31' + 50.37, 52.84, 54.30, 51.45''.
- Weights 6, 4, 2, 1.
- Weighted mean: α = 192°31'51.82'' at the weighted mean clock time 10h47'1.9''. Both check exactly.
- Declination: 1°32'31.59'' at 10h51'14.8''. A reduction of −1.49'' (Juno's motion between the two times) is noted.

(4) BOTTOM: Lalande zone of 20 Apr 1796, reduced to 8 Apr 1815.
- For each star the clock time gets a correction of about −31.1 to −31.6 s. This is interpolated in a small table against the instrument reading 44°–46°: −31.60, −31.35, −31.10. It combines clock error with the reduction from the last wire, varying with declination.
- The instrument reading gets the refraction +54.93, +56.89, +58.94''. This table is the tabular log refraction (1.74974 etc.) plus 9.99010, the log of the thermometer factor (12.5°) times the barometer factor (28.1 in).
- All interpolations check, e.g. 35 Vir: 12h38'0.47'' − 31.56 = 37'28.91''; 44°8'45'' + 55.21'' = 44°9'40.21''.
- Reference stars 35 Vir, 37 Vir and δ Vir (the last done on the next page) have catalogue places for 1800, almost certainly Piazzi. These are brought back to 20 Apr 1796:
  - t = 1800 − 1796.301 = 3.699 yr (log 0.56808).
  - Logs of the annual variations: 35 Vir 1.65963 / 1.29732 (45.66'', 19.83''); 37 Vir 1.66068 / 1.29535. These presumably include proper motion.
  - 35 Vir: 189°25'6.60'' − 2'48.93'' = 189°22'17.67''; δ: 4°40'4.30'' + 1'13.35'' = 4°41'17.65''.
  - Adding 1796 aberration and nutation: apparent 189°22'18.98'' = 12h37m29.27s, δ = 4°41'18.71''.
  - 37 Vir: 190°18'44.81'' = 12h41m14.99s, δ = 4°10'5.27''.
- Clock corrections: Corr AR = catalogue − observed = +0.36 s (35 Vir) and +0.59 s (37 Vir); with δ Vir's +0.14 s from the next page the mean is +0.36 s.
- Instrument zero: reading + declination gives 48°50'58.93'', 48°51'1.50'', 48°50'59.65''. The mean, 48°51'0.03'', is the instrument zero.
- Stars a and b:
  - a: δ = 48°51'0.03'' − 45°47'45.48'' = 3°3'14.55''; α = 12h42m10.41s.
  - b: δ = 3°13'38.91''; α = 12h42m29.16s.
  - These are the inputs reduced to 1815 on the next page.

PURPOSE: obtain 1815 apparent places of faint comparison stars, and from them Juno positions, for Gauss's orbit work.
errors: Star c, 1796 mean RA: 31.95 − 17.71 + 16.00 + 0.02 = 30.26'', but Gauss writes 30.22'' (0.04'' slip; the declination column is correct).

Star c, 1815 aberration in RA: the log sum 1.2689 (1.2699 + 9.9989 + 0.0001) corresponds to 18.57'', but 18.75 is written (digit transposition). With this and the previous slip, c apparent RA should be about 193°9'2.30'' instead of 193°9'2.44''. The error may propagate into Juno's RA 'aus c'.

37 Virginis: log sin δ and log tan δ are written 8.8572 / 8.8583. For δ = 4°10'4'' they should be about 8.8614 / 8.8626, a slip of 0.004 in the log. The effect on the 0.54'' and 0.08'' terms is ≤ 0.01''.
35 Virginis declination: the constant aberration term is entered as −3.23 and −3.60 (bracketed, apparently a correction), total −6.83''. The expected value is about −6.85''; this is negligible.
Everything else checks: the precession log products, the Juno weighted means, the zone-table interpolations, the instrument zero, and the derived places of a and b.

results.what: Reduction of apparent star places between epochs via annual aberration (Bessel-type day-number form with auxiliary angle ☉') and nutation (auxiliary angle ☊'), evaluated logarithmically
results.modern_name: Reduction from mean to apparent place (aberration + nutation day numbers)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (aberration, nutation); auxiliary-angle tables by Gauss (published c. 1808 in Zach's Monatliche Correspondenz) and later Bessel's day numbers (1820s)

results.what: Precession in α, δ over 18.94 yr using values at the mean epoch: Δα = m t + n t sin α_m tan δ_m, Δδ = n t cos α_m
results.modern_name: Precession in right ascension and declination (mid-epoch / first-order formula)

results.what: Reduction of Lalande's Histoire Céleste zone observations: clock and wire correction, refraction, instrument zero fixed from catalogue stars
results.modern_name: Zone-star reduction (later systematized in Bessel's 1825 tables and Baily's 1847 catalogue)

results.what: Weighted mean of Juno RA from four comparison stars, weights 6:4:2:1, with the time averaged by the same weights

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observational reduction (aberration, nutation, precession, zone reduction, weighted mean) of comparison stars for Juno in 1815, using Gauss's own published aberration/nutation scheme. It is well within the known practice of Gauss and his contemporaries; only small arithmetic slips are of note.
